title: This Week's Hottest AI Papers on arXiv

sections.title: ExplorationBench: Measuring AI Systems' Exploration in Verifiable Alien Worlds
sections.abstract: Introduces two executable, unfamiliar alien-world sandboxes that test whether AI systems can discover and apply new rules rather than recall training data.
sections.claimed_contribution: A verifiable benchmark separating exploration from memorization.
sections.caveat: Synthetic environments may not transfer directly to open-ended scientific discovery.

sections.title: SAGE: Mitigating Long-Horizon Reasoning Biases via Topological Guidance
sections.abstract: Presents structural guidance combining algebraic sparsification and hyperbolic state representations to reduce exploration and compounding biases in long-horizon reasoning.
sections.claimed_contribution: Symbolic Closure Analysis and the SAGE framework.
sections.caveat: The strongest reported result is task-specific and component-level attribution is unclear from the abstract.

sections.title: Self-Play Pretraining with Zero Data
sections.abstract: Studies generator-learner self-play from random initialization, using computable synthetic sequences as an adaptive curriculum.
sections.claimed_contribution: A proof-of-concept for self-play pretraining over a universal-computation-inspired search space.
sections.caveat: The work is an initial proof of concept without established competitive natural-language performance.

sections.title: Synthetic Hospital: An Open, Verifiable, Physician-Validated Longitudinal EHR Benchmark
sections.abstract: Releases a synthetic, provenance-linked longitudinal EHR benchmark with 1,268 patients and 5,602 encounters through a simulated hospital-record system.
sections.claimed_contribution: An open, fact-grounded, physician-validated clinical benchmark.
sections.caveat: Synthetic records may not represent the full distribution of real clinical workflows and populations.

sections.title: Qwen-Planner-Agent: A Closed-Loop AI-for-AI Framework for Real-World Mobile Planner Agents
sections.abstract: Connects agentic data generation, training, deployment, execution evidence, and model-harness co-evolution for mobile planning agents.
sections.claimed_contribution: A closed-loop AI-for-AI framework with a shared action-feedback-verification contract and CARE reward engineering.
sections.caveat: Deployment cost and independence from the authors' evaluation harness are not clear from the abstract.

sections.title: C3M: Cross-Session Multimodal Memory Maintenance for Long-Horizon Tasks
sections.abstract: Maintains a bounded active index over persistent text-image evidence and routes source expansion under a fixed reader budget.
sections.claimed_contribution: Relation-aware multimodal memory updates with provenance-preserving query-time routing.
sections.caveat: The abstract provides no numerical comparison against competing memory systems.

sections.title: JEV vs. LLMs as Rubric Judges: Cheaper, Faster, and Wrong in the Same Places
sections.abstract: Compares a typed probabilistic classifier with three LLM judges across nine panels, finding major cost and latency advantages but correlated errors.
sections.claimed_contribution: An empirical analysis of cheap judge substitution and cascade limits.
sections.caveat: The tested judge families and panels may not represent broader evaluation regimes.
